title: Which engine is most efficient in token usage?
author: ETZEEA
selftext: I want to know since Godot is the lightest, but Unity have the most support with CLI able to use 1000+ tools, where unreal engine i dont see much update with it.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body:
three.js is not a game engine.

It is efficient for building prototypes of anything graphical, but beyond that, you are basically building from scratch.

replies.author: PastaSaladOverdose
replies.body:
Which is totally fine because 1. There's prob an open source library out there that already does what you need and 2. It costs absolutely nothing to code with it using Claude. We're talking medium effort Opus 5.5 churning out crazy results. 

He's asking for efficient token usage - my vote is Typescript/three.js/next.js

comments.author: Templeshooter
comments.body: I use Bevy and build my tooling around it, eventually i have lots of project i can borrow from one another, like for example i come up with debug panel and now every demo i make has it, in-game world editor accessible from that panel is another feature, there is cool looking floating combat text and do on. Since its all code, ai can handle every part of it, it can integrate auto-play to test features visually. You don't have to install giant applications like the unreal editor.

comments.author: toroidalvoid
comments.body: You should probably run the evaluation yourself. Think of a sample scene or game similar to what you want to build and build it using the different tools you are considering and track the token use

comments.author: tindalos
comments.body: I like defold and rive for vector deformation.  But I’m going to prototype in bevy also.

comments.author: ContDev
comments.body: made my first mobile game in unity with ai doing a lot of the boring code and tbh the engine matters less than what you let it read. unity scene/prefab files are huge yaml so if the ai keeps poking at those it burns tokens fast, keeping it in plain c# scripts and wiring stuff in the editor yourself stays pretty cheap. godot's text scenes are way lighter if you want it editing scenes directly tho

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I would bet on Unity here.

Your code will be straight C# and it is very token-efficient to write C#.

The engine itself has a ton of features you might want, so the AI does not have to implement them for you.

Godot is probably also a good choice, but GDScript can be a little annoying to work with because the type checking does not give good feedback (and this can require more thinking from the LLM, too).

I would stay away from e.g. Three.js, Bevy if you want to be efficient.
